title: Mumbai gourmet-chocolate D2C cut peak-season dependence 64% to 49% by manufacturing year-round consumption occasions
content: SITUATION: A Mumbai gourmet-chocolate D2C booked 64% of its ₹9.2 Cr annual revenue in just three gifting months — October (Diwali), December and February (Valentine's). June-August averaged ₹38L/month against ₹1.9 Cr in October. Cash froze in lean months while we burned ₹14L/month retargeting a tapped-out gifting audience on Meta at a punishing ₹640 CAC. The trap was occasion, not product: nobody buys a ₹899 gift box for themselves on a Tuesday. ACTION: We stopped fighting for gifting share and built non-gifting demand. We launched a ₹349 'self-treat' 6-piece pack and listed it on Zepto and Blinkit across Mumbai, Pune and Bengaluru for impulse buying. We ran a ₹599/month 'chocolate of the month' WhatsApp subscription to 41,000 past buyers, and rebuilt Meta Advantage+ around micro-occasions — 'monsoon comfort', Rakhi, Friendship Day — instead of two mega-festivals. OUTCOME: Over 7 months lean-month revenue rose ₹38L to ₹71L (+87%). Quick-commerce reached 22% of revenue. The subscription converted 7.6% of past buyers — 3,100 recurring members at ₹18.5L MRR. Blended CAC fell ₹640 to ₹410, and peak three-month concentration dropped 64% to 49%.
lesson: For a seasonal product, don't widen the funnel — change the occasion. Seasonality is a positioning problem, not a media-spend problem: retargeting a gifting audience in June just bids up CAC against demand that isn't there. Manufacture small, frequent, low-ticket consumption moments — a sub-₹400 self-treat pack, a WhatsApp subscription, quick-commerce impulse on Zepto and Blinkit — so revenue stops being hostage to two calendar dates you can't move.
